partner_result_applied.name: affine-family finite-mixture localization compiler
partner_result_applied.actual_use: After proving for each arbitrary target matrix A that every compact finite-fragment affine product law obeys P{P_A in I}<=C_genff|I| by generic-matrix approximation, applied the partner finite-mixture compiler to obtain the identical inequality for every arbitrary cap-one product law, with the same affine parameters and no support/fragment/moment tax.

proved.statement: The optimal interval-concentration constant for the full affine target class (all cap-one product laws; symmetric A with three |lambda|>=1) equals exactly the optimal constant restricted to compact finite-fragment indicator product laws and invertible simple-spectrum matrices with three |lambda|>1. The same equality holds in the homogeneous l=c=0 class.
Physical-coordinate translations preserve the affine class exactly via l->l+2Ah and c->c+l^Th+h^TAh, with no density-cap or finite-fragment cost.

remaining_implication: The full target still requires a product-preserving smoothing theorem in the no-pivot/grouped-bank/non-coloop regime. Localization can now be postponed: it suffices for essential boundedness to solve that analytic/structural step on generic strict-spectrum matrices and compact finite-fragment product inputs with a constant independent of their support geometry.
